proposition: In letter 20 (ca. 829/1426) Ibn Turka told Shāhrukh that his aim in serving the Sharīʿa was to be blameless before the Prophet and to further Shāhrukh's own Sharīʿa-promoting mission, said he had sent a darvīsh to court to discuss matters to that end, and sent with the letter a treatise on the occult properties of things and occult sciences that he thought the ruler should find interesting.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to Shāhrukh (heading given by MK as 'Amīrzāda Shāhrukh')
mediation.note: Letters to third parties ask or offer favours; the text survives only in copies made after his lifetime (except the marginal letters in MS Majlis 10196).

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, summarising, dating and identifying the letter(s)
mediation.note: MK's heading calls Shāhrukh 'Amīrzāda' though the letter calls him sultan; see notes
